heading.text: Prepare your application and core documents

source_wording.text:
Prepare the completed amendment application (Form D.R.P/1,7,8), the previously used National Identity card, a birth certificate or a birth-register extract certified by the Additional District Registrar, and an ICAO-standard photograph taken within the last 6 months.

concise.text: Prepare the completed application, your old NIC, your birth certificate and a recent photograph.

detailed.text: Prepare the completed amendment application (Form D.R.P/1,7,8), the National Identity card you have been using, a birth certificate or a birth-register extract certified by the Additional District Registrar, and an ICAO-standard photograph taken within the last 6 months. These are the documents everyone needs; the next step covers extra evidence some people must add.

text.text: The department's page links the application form (Form D.R.P/1,7,8) as a download.

recap.text: You looked at the core documents for the application.

heading.text: Check whether you need extra evidence

source_wording.text:
Some applicants must add further evidence: a probable age certificate or register search results with proof of name and date of birth if there is no birth certificate; an affidavit, recognised written evidence and register search results for applicants over 40 with neither; a citizenship certificate for those born abroad to a Sri Lankan parent; a dual citizenship certificate where it applies; clergy documents where they apply; and an attested marriage certificate when using a husband's name or surname.

concise.text: Add extra evidence only if one of the listed circumstances applies to you.

detailed.text: The core documents are enough unless one of these circumstances applies: you have no birth certificate, you were born abroad to a Sri Lankan parent, you hold dual citizenship, you are clergy, or you want to use a husband's name or surname. Each case has its own document, shown on the card with the circumstance it belongs to.

text.text: An applicant who has a birth certificate and none of the other listed circumstances adds nothing more to the core documents.

recap.text: You looked at which extra evidence applies to different circumstances.

concise.text: Forward your application through the Estate Superintendent and pay the fee there.

text.text: Every applicant must forward the application through the certifying officer, so applying directly to the department is not an alternative for the normal service.
